title: First Swedish tour: concerts, flowers, and Alice Babs
summary: Armstrong recalls his first Stockholm concerts, the crowds at the station, a reporter's question about Swedish girls, Jack Teagarden at the concert hall, and Alice Babs singing with the band.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: One of our biggest successes in Stockholm, you know what I mean? I remember the first time we went there, I was booked in there by a new serial by the name of Mr. Edwald and Mr. Scarrick from Copenhagen, Denmark. They gave me three concerts at night. Our band, Mary Alice and the Gypsy Girls. And all the houses sold out. And after the concert, they had to go in the dining room of my hotel, which is a beautiful hotel that runs all over Europe because my wife traveled with me and everything. And we'd sit down there and have a wonderful time. And I'll never forget that. And then the first time in Sweden, there were so many people at the station. They gave me a trumpet of flowers and the so many things, the flowers crumbled up and I had to make a beeline back to the train. And they were wonderful. And there were people in Stockholm there and one of the sun see them or two. I remember those newspapers, Man by Page, you two cats, you know. He got a, he asked me a funny question or a question. He said, uh, there's something strong. He said, what do you think of our beautiful Swedish girls? You know. I said, well I tell you, my wife travels with me. She travels with me all the time. And she's got the best smorgasbord in the world. And I'll never forget all Sweden. We played in the cottage party. And that's that concert over there, that beautiful piano, that sound. And during intermission, we were standing outside with our collars up, you know, kind of, people get cold. And there was three of his boys come up to Jack Tay Garden and he says, you photo for me. And Jack said, well I tell you, I live two blocks from the concert hall. He said, yeah. He said, yeah. He said, yeah. He said, now, if I go there, I'll catch cold, you know. He said, yeah. He said, yeah. He said, you wouldn't want me to catch cold. He said, yeah. And he remember Alice Babs. Oh yeah. Well, that's the girl that got our inspiration the first night she sang with us in Stockholm. She sang about three or four numbers in this world of the house. And now she's in America doing wonderful. And we're talking about those moments. I've been talking about Sweden, you know. I'm done.
